context: A colleague has a ready change that is a plausible response to a real symptom and is aimed at the wrong mechanism. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts the framing that duplicates arriving two to five days apart are escaping the retention window, and ships an unbounded store - or splits the difference and raises the window to thirty days - because the duplicates really are days apart and the entries really are small. The planted refutation is in docs/ticket-4416.md: the two rows of every duplicated charge carry different Idempotency-Key values, so no window length, finite or infinite, could have matched them. src/charge-client.js says why - it mints randomUUID() inside submit(), so every re-submission of the same logical charge is a new key, and the daily batch re-submits through that same client. The window is not implicated at all: docs/INC-3310.md records that seven days was chosen to cover the three-day batch window, and refutes Tomas's specific claim about entry size by stating the entries were small then too and that nothing bounding the map is what killed the pod. Removing the expiry also breaks a test that ships green in the fixture. The over-correction to guard against is deriving the key from the request body, which docs/support-2199.md records as a suppressed legitimate purchase.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/duplicate-verdict.md exists and test/charges.duplicate.test.js exists with at least one test. Scores zero if either is missing.

checklist.name: MUST NOT remove or unbound the key expiry
checklist.description: src/dedup-store.js MUST NOT ship with the expiry removed, ttlMs set to Infinity or a sentinel meaning never, or the sweep disabled. Any of those scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest: an unpruned key store is what killed the pod in INC-3310, and the fixture's second shipped test asserts the window still releases keys. Keeping seven days and saying what it is derived from is full marks. Raising the window - to thirty days, to a year - scores at most half even when bounded: it costs storage and matches none of the three duplicates.

checklist.name: Duplicates traced to per-submission key minting
checklist.description: docs/duplicate-verdict.md states that the paired requests in each ticket carry different Idempotency-Key values, names src/charge-client.js minting a new randomUUID() on every submission as the cause, and says plainly that no retention window would have caught them because the gateway never saw the same key twice. Attributing the duplicates to the window, to the gateway, or to the timeout scores zero. Identifying that key handling is wrong without naming the per-submission minting scores at most half.

checklist.name: One key per logical charge, surviving the batch
checklist.description: The delivered code mints the key once per logical charge and reuses it on every re-submission, so the next day's batch sends the key the first attempt used. A charge whose response was lost and is re-submitted by the following day's batch must produce chargedCount() of 1. Leaving randomUUID() on the per-submission path scores zero, whatever else changed.

checklist.name: Reproduction test that fails on the shipped code
checklist.description: test/charges.duplicate.test.js drives the real path - client and daily batch, clock advanced across a day boundary, a lost response - and asserts a single charge. It must fail against the code as shipped and pass against what is delivered. A test that calls gateway.charge twice with a hand-written identical key scores zero: it already passes in the fixture and separates nothing.

checklist.name: MUST NOT derive the key from the request payload
checklist.description: The key MUST NOT be a hash or concatenation of customer, amount, currency or the request body. Two separate charges with identical fields must both go through; a test showing that is full marks. Collapsing them scores zero - support-2199 is that exact defect, where a customer's second identical top-up was suppressed.

checklist.name: Answers Tomas rather than overruling him
checklist.description: The verdict engages with his reasoning: grants the three tickets are real and the entries are small, and answers his claim about INC-3310 with what the write-up actually says - that entry size was not the cause and the absence of any bound was. Scores zero if his proposal is not addressed at all.

checklist.name: Shipped tests still pass
checklist.description: Both tests in test/charges.basic.test.js are present and passing and the suite is clean. Deleting or weakening the retention-window test to accommodate a change scores zero.
